data.gender_notes: Mishu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Mata' meaning mother and 'Ishu' meaning God. Mishu is a name for a little goddess or divine being. In Hindu mythology, Mishu represents compassion, nurturing, and love. The name Mishu carries the meaning “Little Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mishu usually hope their child will grow to embody little goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace divine femininity and nurturing energy.
data.etymology: Mishu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mishu total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: According to the Puranic texts, Mishu was a demon king who ruled over the region of Anga in ancient India. He was a powerful asura, capable of assuming various forms and had a large following. Mishu is known for his role in the Mahabharata, where he was vanquished by Bhima, the strongest of the Pandava brothers. This event is believed to have occurred during the Mahabharata war, which took place in the 4th century BCE.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Mishu can be found in the Jataka tales, which are a collection of Buddhist stories popular in ancient India. In one of these tales, Mishu is described as a wealthy merchant who lived in the city of Takshila. He was known for his generosity and kindness towards all living beings. One day, Mishu came across a starving and sick monkey, who was about to die. Mishu took pity on the monkey and fed him, offering him shelter and medical care. The monkey, who was actually the future Buddha in disguise, was so grateful for Mishu's kindness that he blessed him with happiness and prosperity. This story is believed to have taken place during the 3rd century BCE.
